P31 ([[D-C-GNU-STATEMENT-EXPRESSION]]): the runnable witness for the GNU `({ ... })` statement expression. ★★ BORN AGAINST A REFUSAL: ✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI at HEAD 60198126, `int m = ({ int _a=(a); _a; });` failed with `error[P0009]: expected 'Identifier', 'IntLiteral', 'FloatLiteral', … — got '{'` at the brace.
★★ THE SUBSTRATE ALREADY EXISTED, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ROW: the construct lowers onto `HirKind::SeqExpr` ([stmts…, result]), whose own header comment in hir_node.hpp names GCC statement expressions as what it models. It was built as the carrier for value-yielding `++`, assignment-as-a-value and complex-lvalue compound-assign; MIR's SeqExpr arm already runs each statement child through `lowerStmt` (an ARBITRARY statement, not just an assignment) and `collectLocalDecls` already walks the WHOLE body subtree, so a declaration nested inside an expression already gets its entry-block Alloca. ZERO new HIR kinds, ZERO MIR change, ZERO LIR change — only the front end was missing, and the fix is a grammar rule plus one CST→HIR lowering.
★ WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW: ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 over /usr/include (C headers only, the C++ tree excluded, every pattern carrying a positive control) — 59 occurrences across 15 headers, including `assert.h`, `math.h`, `ctype.h`, `unistd.h`, `netinet/in.h`, `bits/stdio.h`, `bits/select2.h`, `bits/cpu-set.h`. SEVEN of those sites are written `__extension__ ({`, which is why SHAPE 12 is here and why this row and D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD are one cycle's work: with only one of them landed, `math.h` and `assert.h` WERE still refused. Both landed in P31, so that is NO LONGER true — ✔MEASURED in P31, a 1819-line `gcc -E -P` glibc TU parses with zero errors from either construct.
★★ THE TWO REFUSALS THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONTAIN, because they are refusals and belong in the ctest pins: a VOID statement expression used where a value is required (S_StatementExprHasNoValue) and one at FILE scope (S_StatementExprAtFileScope). BOTH are refused by gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 19.1.7 too (✔MEASURED: `void value not ignored as it ought to be` / `braced-group within expression allowed only inside a function`), so neither is a DSS-only narrowing. SHAPE 9 is the void form in the position both references ACCEPT — a discard — and it is written so a lowering that dropped the body changes the ANSWER (`k` is read afterwards) rather than merely losing a value.
⚠ THE `volatile` SEED IS LOAD-BEARING, and this is the same trap `asm_goto_labels` records: without it the release pipeline folds every shape to a constant before MIR is ever asked to run the statements, and the file exits 42 while testing nothing. ⚠ SHAPE 3 (the same macro used TWICE in one function) is the discriminating case for the scope: `stmtExpr` is a `semantics.scopes` rule, and without that the second use either redeclares `_a` or reads the first use's temporary.
★ THE `release` ARM is where SHAPES 6, 7 and 9 earn their place: an assignment / post-increment / void body whose statements the optimizer must not treat as dead. A baseline-only corpus would let a pass that mistook SeqExpr's statement children for pure expressions ship green.
